newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy steps up border controls for British beef.
newsitem.headline: Italy steps up border controls for British beef.

text.p: Italy said on Friday it had stepped up border controls to ensure no British beef entered the country following reports that some British meat producers had managed to evade a beef export ban.
"(There has been) an increase in controls on the border which allow us to stop the import of live cattle, meat and animal meal from Britain," the Health Ministry said in a statement.
The European Commission said on Thursday that 1,600 tonnes of British beef had illegally been exported to the Netherlands, Russia and Egypt despite a ban imposed because of the mad cow crisis.

"We don't intend to lower our guard," Health Minister Rosy Bindi said in the statement. "But this new emergency confirms the urgency of improving Community rules to allow the maximum protection of consumers."

The statement said the latest tightening of controls, which took effect on Wednesday, would add to measures already implemented on imports from Ireland, France and Portugal. It said similar measures would be introduced for imports from Switzerland.
British beef exports were banned in March 1996 to protect consumer health after Britain said it was possible a human form of mad cow disease, CJD, could be caught from eating infected beef.
